root_idea.summary: The root has two principal orientations: weakness or inability, and the rear or latter part of a thing.
root_idea.development: The sense of falling behind or reaching the end develops into incapacity to attain or accomplish something. A separate branch names the hinder part or end, with extensions to bodily, material, and figurative rear portions.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural is presented under the supported singular citation form عَجُزٌ.
The Quranic plural active participle is presented under its singular citation form مُعَاجِزٌ.
The Quranic active participle is presented under its singular citation form مُعْجِزٌ.

senses.definition: To be unable; to lack the strength, power, or ability to do, attain, or accomplish something.
senses.usage_conditions: Form I, commonly construed with عَنْ for inability with respect to an act or object. The Quranic occurrence presents inability to perform an act.

senses.definition: To render unable to reach, overtake, or accomplish something; in the corresponding intransitive or inverted construction, to fail to reach or escape.
senses.usage_conditions: Form IV. In the Quranic constructions, the object is not able to evade or escape divine power, or is unable to cause failure in its attainment.

senses.definition: The rear, hinder part, or latter end of a thing; in the Quranic expression أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ, the trunks or stems of palm trees.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the plural أَعْجَازُ. The sense extends from a thing's rear portion to its latter or terminal part; in the cited simile it denotes palm trunks.

senses.definition: An aged or very old woman.
senses.usage_conditions: A feminine noun; the Quranic occurrences refer to a woman advanced in age, with old age conventionally associated with diminished strength.

senses.definition: One who opposes or contests, striving to outstrip or frustrate the Prophet's party; one who acts as though he could render them unable or evade the divine command.
senses.usage_conditions: Active participle of Form III, attested in the Quran in the plural مُعَاجِزِينَ. The interpretation includes opposing, striving for precedence, and imagining that the opposing party can be rendered unable or escaped. The associated resultative wording can describe being outstripped.

senses.definition: One able to escape, evade, or elude; one who can frustrate another's ability to attain or overcome.
senses.usage_conditions: Active participle of Form IV, especially in the construction بِمُعْجِزِينَ. Quranic contexts deny that people can escape or evade divine power.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Being or becoming behind, behindhand, or backward with respect to something; holding back or abstaining from it, especially at the latter part or end of an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A primary verbal-noun sense distinct from the direct Quranic inability use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become aged, especially said of a woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense is explained through the association of old age with loss of strength; it is a verbal use, not merely the noun for an old woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become, or be, large in the hinder parts; of a woman, to be broad or heavy about the hips and posterior.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily description, separate from the general sense of inability.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A high or elevated piece of sand, especially an oblong, fertile sand formation resembling firm ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative topographical use derived from the form or appearance of a large rear portion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be importuned or pressed by someone begging for one's property; one so importuned.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive or resultative use, distinct from inability.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To attribute or impute inability to someone, to deem or make someone unable; hence to withhold, keep back, or divert someone from a person or thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II causative usage; the withholding sense is explained as making attainment impossible.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a travel bag or pack upon a beast of burden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form II construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a poet, to utter or write the last foot of a verse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical poetic use of Form II.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incline to a trusted person and have recourse to him for refuge or protection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III construction with إِلَى; the related expression can describe turning from truth to falsehood for protection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a group, to leave one thing and begin another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional Form III use describing a change of activity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ride upon the hinder part or rump of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V construction with the camel as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease in the hinder part of a horse or similar animal that makes it heavy or sluggish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An animal-health term, distinct from ordinary inability.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The old age of a woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A simple noun for the state of being an old woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression رَكِبَ أَعْجَازَ الإِبِلِ, to expose oneself to abasement, difficulty, and sustained exertion in seeking something; more broadly, to remain dependent on or behind others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic extension of the rear-of-a-camel sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The last foot or latter hemistich of a verse; by extension, the latter part of a rhymed clause or word.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical poetic and rhetorical use, contrasted with صَدْرٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The last child born to a man's or couple's parents, especially one born after the parents have become old.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression ابن العِجْزَةِ denotes a child born in such circumstances.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man's wife, whether old or young; by the corresponding convention, a husband may also be called by the related age title.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a relational conventional use and does not require that the spouse actually be old.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An extremely old or aged man, or an old and weak man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical usage extends the term beyond its common feminine application.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Old wine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical designation based on the wine's age.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular nail in the hilt of a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized technical term associated with another nail called الكَلْبُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sword blade, or a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical use distinct from the age-related meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A named period of severe late-winter days, traditionally counted as five or seven days, sometimes associated with the destructive wind of ʿĀd.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional calendrical expression; accounts differ over the number and names of the days.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who is impotent with women; also a stallion unable to cover.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized sexual and animal-breeding use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The backtoe of a bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lacking strength, power, or ability; powerless, unable, or impotent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ordinary active-participle adjective of the basic inability branch, not a separate Quranic form group here.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a garment, too short, narrow, or scanty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical application of inability to provide sufficient coverage or extent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An eagle deficient or short in the tail, or marked by a distinctive whiteness or coloration in its hinder part.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive term with variant zoological explanations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pillow-like pad used by a woman to enlarge the appearance of her hinder part.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A cosmetic or clothing-related object, also reported under a related vocalization.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A miracle associated with a prophet that disables opponents by making them unable to produce its like; in theology, an extraordinary event supporting a prophetic claim.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical theological term, distinct from the active participle مُعْجِزٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A zone or waist-belt worn next to the wearer's hinder part.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized clothing term named in relation to عَجُز.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who is habitually or constantly lacking strength or ability; perpetually unable or impotent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive nominal pattern.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical item with no further semantic restriction supplied.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form III racing and outstripping belong to the Quran-attested contesting branch.
Outstripping or fleeing beyond pursuit is covered by the contesting branch.
Pointer to the related عاجز entry.
Editorial statement without a lexical definition.
Grammatical cross-reference to the feminine form.
Explicit Quranic interpretation of the active participle.
The result of being outstripped belongs to the same contesting and outstripping branch.
Explicit Quranic interpretation of the canonical Form III participle.

cautions: Lane and Mufradat report an alternate Quran reading مُعَجِّزِينَ, interpreted as hindering or attributing impotence to the Prophet's followers. It is not assigned to the canonical QAC form group مُعَاجِزِينَ because its morphology differs.
A Lane Quran citation is preserved only as lexical evidence where relevant; its historical citation notation has not been converted into an additional modern verse location.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The alternate reading مُعَجِّزِينَ discussed for the passages represented by مُعَاجِزِينَ is outside the supplied canonical QAC form group and is therefore recorded as a variant rather than as a separate public Quranic form.
